3. Recommendations for legality due diligence in the 
context of national coffee production
Land-use rights
1.1.1 Land tenure is well-defined and respected
1.1.2 Agriculture is permitted on the plot.
Environmental protection
2.1.1 Agriculture standards in restricted areas or areas of legal exclusion are respected

2.1.2 and 2.1.4 Only pesticides, herbicides, fertilisers and fungicides authorised by SENASA are used, and waste 
management is carried out
2.1.3 Water resources are protected and used in accordance with the law
2.1.5 Soils are managed in accordance with the law
2.2.1 Forest conversion complies with legal requirements

2.2.3 Legal requirements for biodiversity conservation and the protection of endangered or protected species are 
met
Third parties' rights
3.1.1 The rights of local communities are respected.
3.1.2 Right to claim compensation in the event of damage or injury
3.2.1 Derecho a reclamar una indemnización en caso de daños y perjuicios
3.2.2 Productive activities are not carried out in areas of cultural significance
Labour law*
4.1.1 Type of employment relationship
4.1.2 and 4.1.3 Working hours are respected and remuneration complies with legal requirements
4.1.3 No discrimination on the basis of sex or race, or against migrant workers
4.4.1 Legal requirements regarding health and safety in the workplace are met
Human rights*
5.1.1 Children are not employed below the legal age
5.2.1 Workers are free to terminate their employment relationship with prior notice

5.2.2 No wages, benefits, documents or property are withheld from workers, and no one is subjected to slavery or 
forced labour
5.3.1 There is no sexual harassment or gender discrimination
Free, Prior and Informed Consent
FPIC is obtained when the rights of indigenous peoples or local communities are affected
Tax, customs and anti-corruption standards
7.1.1 Property taxes, value-added taxes, corporate and export taxes, royalties and duties are paid
7.2.1 Customs duties are paid, trade quotas and regulations are complied with
7.2.2 Companies must be legally constituted.
7.3.1 Absence of corrupt practices
